eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket reflects the tight clustering of latest forecast models around a Moscow high of 23–24°C on May 4, driven by a stabilizing high-pressure ridge over European Russia ushering in southerly winds and clear skies for enhanced solar insolation after late-April's cold snap with blizzards and highs below 5°C. The slight edge to 24°C (36.5%) stems from warmer GFS ensemble runs factoring urban heat island effects and maximal afternoon heating, while 23°C (29.5%) aligns with more conservative ECMWF guidance anticipating minor cloud intrusions; 22°C and 25°C trail due to lower model probabilities. Uncertainties persist in boundary-layer mixing and exact wind speeds, with Rosgidromet updates and Vnukovo station observations resolving the market tomorrow. Historical May norms hover near 18°C, underscoring this above-average warmth.

eventMetadata.context_description: A Black Sea-sourced low-pressure system has triggered an unusual May cold snap in Istanbul, dropping temperatures 6-8°C below seasonal norms with persistent light rain and drizzle, driving trader consensus toward mid-teens highs on May 4. Turkish State Meteorological Service (MGM) forecasts a 10-16°C range, but recent observations of 11-12°C daytime temps under heavy cloud cover and 28 km/h northerly winds align market-implied odds with 13°C (42.5%) slightly ahead of 14°C (34%), reflecting uncertainty in cloud thickness and shower timing suppressing daytime heating. Ensemble models like ECMWF and GFS show similar clustering, though brief clearing could nudge toward 14°C; watch MGM's evening update and tomorrow's soundings for shifts before resolution via official station data.

This marks a cooldown from early May warmth, driven by a low-pressure system over central Europe noted in updates over the past 48 hours. New 12Z model outputs today and ARPA Lombardia observations tomorrow could refine cloud cover and boundary layer mixing, key differentiators between outcomes. Historical May 5 highs average 20°C, but current synoptic patterns favor subdued temperatures below climatology.
